questions.q: What is the difference between prefixing a query with EXPLAIN versus PROFILE in Cypher?
options: EXPLAIN shows the planned execution plan without running the query; PROFILE actually executes it and shows real row counts and db hits
EXPLAIN and PROFILE are interchangeable synonyms with identical behavior
PROFILE only works on CREATE statements, never on MATCH
EXPLAIN executes the query twice for accuracy while PROFILE runs it once
questions.explain: EXPLAIN is the estimated-plan equivalent (no execution); PROFILE is the actual-plan equivalent, executing the query and annotating real statistics.

questions.q: What does a NodeByLabelScan operator in a Cypher plan indicate?
options: Neo4j is walking every node with a given label to find matches — the graph equivalent of a SQL Server table/clustered scan
The query used an index successfully
The query has a syntax error
The query only touched relationships, never nodes
questions.explain: NodeByLabelScan means no index was available, so every node with that label had to be checked — directly analogous to a relational table scan.

questions.q: What operator would you expect to see instead of NodeByLabelScan after creating an appropriate index?
options: NodeIndexSeek
NodeByLabelScan would still appear, unchanged
FullGraphTraversal
TableScan
questions.explain: Once an index exists on the filtered property, the planner can use NodeIndexSeek — a direct, sub-linear lookup — instead of scanning every labeled node.

questions.q: What does the following statement do? `CREATE INDEX person_name_index IF NOT EXISTS FOR (p:Person) ON (p.name)`
options: Creates a range index on the name property of Person nodes, speeding up lookups that filter or match on that property
Deletes all Person nodes whose name is not indexed
Creates a new Person node with a name property
Renames the Person label to person_name_index
questions.explain: This is standard Cypher index-creation syntax — it builds an index on Person.name to support faster property lookups.

questions.q: What tradeoff does creating a Cypher index introduce, according to this lesson?
options: Extra write overhead, since every CREATE, SET, or MERGE touching the indexed property now also has to maintain the index
Indexes in Neo4j have no tradeoffs whatsoever
Indexes make all queries slower, with no benefit
Indexes can only be created on relationships, never on node properties
questions.explain: This mirrors the exact same tradeoff relational indexes carry — faster reads at the cost of extra maintenance work on writes.
